hypothesis: The existing upstream PGO/LTO recipe can improve throughput of the original v26 shared objects without changing its compressed stream.
source: original candidate checkout used by the existing v26 experiment; all algorithm macros stay at their original defaults
prerequisite: round234/prefetch/state.json: status=complete; preserve the entire prefetch A/B and reverse-order confirmation

profile.research_main: Original probe main stays non-PGO and non-LTO; shared ordinary objects and final link use upstream PGO/LTO.

resource.cpu_affinity: one available core, identical for all new trials
resource.timeout_policy: remote GNU timeout kills each stage process group; logs and receipts stay on the remote disk

sequence.name: prefix-256k
sequence.purpose: real encode/decode, exact original golden compressed stream

sequence.name: article-q2-1m
sequence.purpose: only after >=3% prefix gain; reverse order on disjoint content

continue_gate: All golden streams and real restorations exact; prefix sum of encode/decode coding seconds improves by at least 3%.
accept_gate: All outputs exactly match original goldens; sum across both 1 MiB pairs improves by at least 3%, with positive q2 gain.
stop: A changed golden stream stops this neutral comparison and retains the separate compile-family files; a failed speed gate stops this recipe. No training-input or compiler-flag sweep.
reporting: Wall/coding time, CPU when emitted by original probe, RSS and executable bytes separately. This is an experimental probe using final shared objects; full S and formal normalized runtime require full-data measurements.
